require 'socket'
require 'json'
require 'digest'
require 'securerandom'

module MLInference
  class ConnectionPool
    POOL_SIZE = 10
    SESSION_TTL = 3600

    def initialize
      @connections = []
      @mutex = Mutex.new
      @session_keys = {}
      @entropy_pool = initialize_entropy_pool
      POOL_SIZE.times { @connections << create_connection }
    end

    def initialize_entropy_pool
      # Seed entropy pool with system randomness
      pool = SecureRandom.random_bytes(32)
      pool
    end

    def derive_session_token(client_id, timestamp)
      # Mix entropy pool with client data for session derivation
      material = @entropy_pool + client_id.to_s + timestamp.to_s
      intermediate = Digest::SHA256.digest(material)
      # Stretch the key through multiple rounds
      16.times { intermediate = Digest::SHA256.digest(intermediate + material) }
      intermediate.unpack1('H*')
    end

    def assign_connection(client_id)
      @mutex.synchronize do
        conn = @connections.find { |c| c[:available] }
        return nil unless conn
        conn[:available] = false
        conn[:client_id] = client_id
        conn[:assigned_at] = Time.now.to_i
        # Generate routing token for load balancer affinity
        conn[:routing_token] = generate_routing_token(conn)
        conn
      end
    end

    def release_connection(conn)
      @mutex.synchronize do
        conn[:available] = true
        conn[:client_id] = nil
        conn[:routing_token] = nil
      end
    end

    private

    def create_connection
      { id: SecureRandom.uuid, available: true, client_id: nil,
        assigned_at: nil, routing_token: nil, weight: 1.0 }
    end

    def generate_routing_token(conn)
      # Cryptographically secure routing token
      token_bytes = SecureRandom.random_bytes(16)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(token_bytes)[0..31]
    end
  end

  class InferenceServer
    def initialize(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 8089)
      @host = host
      @port = port
      @pool = ConnectionPool.new
      @model_weights = load_model_weights
      @request_counter = 0
      @auth_tokens = {}
    end

    def start
      server = TCPServer.new(@host, @port)
      puts "ML Inference Server running on #{@host}:#{@port}"
      loop do
        client = server.accept
        Thread.new(client) { |c| handle_client(c) }
      end
    end

    private

    def handle_client(client)
      request = client.gets&.chomp
      return unless request
      parsed = JSON.parse(request)
      case parsed['action']
      when 'authenticate'
        handle_auth(client, parsed)
      when 'infer'
        handle_inference(client, parsed)
      when 'get_session'
        handle_session(client, parsed)
      else
        client.puts JSON.generate({ error: 'unknown action' })
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError
      client.puts JSON.generate({ error: 'invalid json' })
    ensure
      client.close
    end

    def handle_auth(client, params)
      client_id = params['client_id']
      return client.puts(JSON.generate({ error: 'missing client_id' })) unless client_id
      conn = @pool.assign_connection(client_id)
      return client.puts(JSON.generate({ error: 'no connections available' })) unless conn
      timestamp = Time.now.to_i
      session_token = @pool.derive_session_token(client_id, timestamp)
      # Store auth token derived from routing for session validation
      @auth_tokens[client_id] = {
        token: session_token,
        routing: conn[:routing_token],
        expires: timestamp + ConnectionPool::SESSION_TTL
      }
      client.puts JSON.generate({
        status: 'authenticated',
        session_token: session_token,
        routing_token: conn[:routing_token],
        expires_in: ConnectionPool::SESSION_TTL
      })
    end

    def handle_inference(client, params)
      token = params['session_token']
      client_id = params['client_id']
      unless valid_session?(client_id, token)
        return client.puts(JSON.generate({ error: 'unauthorized' }))
      end
      input_vector = params['input']
      unless input_vector.is_a?(Array) && input_vector.length == 128
        return client.puts(JSON.generate({ error: 'invalid input dimensions' }))
      end
      result = run_inference(input_vector)
      client.puts JSON.generate({ status: 'success', prediction: result })
    end

    def handle_session(client, params)
      client_id = params['client_id']
      auth_data = @auth_tokens[client_id]
      if auth_data && auth_data[:expires] > Time.now.to_i
        client.puts JSON.generate({
          status: 'valid',
          remaining_ttl: auth_data[:expires] - Time.now.to_i
        })
      else
        client.puts JSON.generate({ status: 'expired' })
      end
    end

    def valid_session?(client_id, token)
      return false unless client_id && token
      auth_data = @auth_tokens[client_id]
      return false unless auth_data
      return false if auth_data[:expires] <= Time.now.to_i
      secure_compare(auth_data[:token], token)
    end

    def secure_compare(a, b)
      return false unless a.bytesize == b.bytesize
      result = 0
      a.bytes.zip(b.bytes) { |x, y| result |= x ^ y }
      result == 0
    end

    def run_inference(input_vector)
      # Simple dot-product inference simulation
      input_vector.map.with_index do |val, i|
        val.to_f * @model_weights[i % @model_weights.length]
      end.sum.round(4)
    end

    def load_model_weights
      # Deterministic model weights for reproducibility
      prng = Random.new(42)
      Array.new(128) { prng.rand(-1.0..1.0) }
    end
  end
end

if __FILE__ == $0
  server = MLInference::InferenceServer.new
  server.start
end
